group: T09-AUDIT-CLAIM-WORDING: connective punctuation of a refusal whose identifying elements (the flag, the 64-hex digest) are intact
grounds: Audit unrefuted. Only the closing parenthesis of the parenthetical is lost; the flag and the digest remain and the digest is delimited by the preceding space. The sibling batch T09b asserts the recovery instruction by regex `--supersede-claim\s+([0-9a-f]{64})(?![0-9a-f])` and then supersedes with the extracted value, so the contract that matters (flag + exact digest that works) is held there and does not depend on the `)`; under the mutant the digest is the last token, which an operator copies more safely than `<sha>)` (cli.py compares by equality, so a copied trailing `)` would not match).

group: T09-EQ-NOFOLLOW: O_NOFOLLOW beside O_CREAT|O_EXCL; O_EXCL already refuses a final-component symbolic link
grounds: Equivalence holds. Proof: O_NOFOLLOW only governs the final path component and O_CREAT|O_EXCL already refuses a final component that exists, a symbolic link included, with EEXIST regardless of its target: POSIX open(), the macOS open(2) man page on this host (`If O_EXCL is set with O_CREAT and the last component of the pathname is a symbolic link, open() will fail even if the symbolic link points to a non-existent name`), Linux open(2), and (recalled, not readable here) Linux build_open_flags ORing O_NOFOLLOW in for O_CREAT|O_EXCL. Where os has no O_NOFOLLOW (Windows) getattr(os,'O_NOFOLLOW',0) is already 0, the mutant's value. The only handler is `except FileExistsError` at L148, and EEXIST is what every state gives. Separate observation, not this mutant (see issues): a dangling link as the NEWEST generation raises a raw FileNotFoundError at L126 (path.read_bytes()), not through os.open.

group: T09-AUDIT-CLAIM-BYTES: the claim file's bytes are only parsed as JSON or hashed as read; nothing re-derives or compares them
grounds: Audit unrefuted. Only the order of keys in the file differs (insertion order fixed in claim(): run, claimed, claimant, supersedes; nested supersedes is not alphabetical either). Bytes are deterministic in both forms; json.loads and every dict comparison are order-insensitive; the digest is of the bytes on disk. The dict returned (and embedded in RUN.json, canonicalised by _content_sha with sort_keys) is the same object in both forms. No document states a canonical byte form of the claim file and nothing re-serialises a claim.

group: T08-UL-EQ-SEQ: indexes 41 and 60 change only the `seq` entry (its presence / its key) of the temporary event dicts built at lineage.py:313 and handed to usage.usage.
grounds: usage.usage (usage.py:75-110) reads the event dicts at exactly two places: e['type'] (usage.py:94, :95) and e['data'] (usage.py:95); it never enumerates a dict's keys, items or copies it, and its return dict (count, sessions, tokens, preflight, retries, wall_s, cost) holds no event.
